label: Neighbourhood amenity score (0-100)
provenance: Amenity point locations pulled from OpenStreetMap and assigned to communities by point-in-polygon against the dashboard's own community boundaries. OSM is crowd-sourced, so completeness varies between districts.
method: Five everyday-amenity densities per km2 - dining, grocery, retail, banking and sports facilities - each percentile-ranked across the communities that have a usable area figure, then averaged into a 0-100 score. Deliberately built from RETAIL AND LEISURE texture rather than infrastructure, so it complements the Livability Score (walkability, transport, healthcare, green space, schools, safety) instead of repeating it.
limitation: A RELATIVE ranking against other Dubai communities, not an absolute standard: 50 means mid-table, not 'adequate'. Density per km2 means large, sparsely developed communities score low even where their built-up core is well served. OSM coverage is uneven, so a low score can reflect thin mapping as well as thin amenities.
